primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Autonomous aldosterone excess increases epithelial sodium-channel activity and basolateral Na+-K+ ATPase activity in collecting-duct principal cells, increasing sodium reabsorption and creating conditions that enhance renal potassium secretion; volume expansion suppresses renin and hydrogen-ion loss contributes to metabolic alkalosis.
vignette: An adult has resistant hypertension, hypokalemia, and metabolic alkalosis. Plasma aldosterone is elevated and plasma renin activity is suppressed.
lead: Which renal transport change most directly contributes to the hypokalemia in this disorder?
correct: Increased epithelial sodium-channel-mediated sodium reabsorption in principal cells, enhancing potassium secretion into the lumen
distractors: Reduced epithelial sodium-channel activity causing diminished lumen-negative potential
Loss of NKCC2 activity causing loop-diuretic-like salt wasting
Loss of the distal Na+-Cl− cotransporter causing reduced distal sodium delivery
Reduced basolateral Na+-K+ ATPase activity in collecting-duct principal cells
distractor_notes: Reduced ENaC activity would reduce rather than promote aldosterone-driven potassium secretion.
NKCC2 loss causes Bartter syndrome with secondary hyperaldosteronism; it is not the direct collecting-duct response to autonomous aldosterone excess.
Loss of the distal Na+-Cl− cotransporter causes Gitelman syndrome and does not describe aldosterone's direct principal-cell action.
Aldosterone increases, rather than reduces, principal-cell sodium transport machinery including Na+-K+ ATPase activity.
key_expl: Aldosterone acts on principal cells to increase ENaC-mediated sodium entry and Na+-K+ ATPase activity. Increased sodium reabsorption makes the tubular lumen relatively negative and, together with increased intracellular potassium delivery from Na+-K+ ATPase, promotes potassium secretion through apical potassium channels. Autonomous aldosterone therefore causes hypertension, hypokalemia, metabolic alkalosis, and renin suppression.
objective: Connect primary aldosteronism with increased principal-cell ENaC activity and enhanced renal potassium secretion.
